sections.h2: Where is the Lucas County Recorder, and how do I submit a deed?
sections.html:
The Lucas County Recorder works from One Government Center, Suite 700, in downtown Toledo, OH 43604. The Recorder's page gives 419-213-4400 for the counter and Recorder@co.lucas.oh.us for email, with weekday hours of 8 AM to 4:30 PM. Electronic recording stops at 4 PM.

Three submission routes are listed: walk it in, mail it, or e-record through a partner company. The office says it strongly encourages electronic recording or mailing, and it names CSC, ePN and Simplifile as the e-recording partners. If you mail a deed, include a self addressed stamped envelope or add return postage to the payment. The fee page accepts cash or a check payable to the Lucas County Recorder.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Lucas County?
sections.html:
The Lucas County recording fee schedule sets the basic fee at $39.00 for the first two pages of a deed or mortgage, and $8.00 for every extra page. The Recorder's news item says the $5.00 increase behind that figure took effect April 1, 2026 under Senate Bill 94, and the schedule lists $39.00 as a minimum.

Selected lines from the Lucas County Recorder fee schedule
ItemAmount shown
Deed or mortgage, first two pages$39.00 minimum
Each additional page$8.00
Non-compliant document (ORC 317.114)$20.00 per document
Reference for a marginal notation (release, assignment)$4.00 per reference
Real estate UCC filing$12.00 plus $4.00 per name indexed
Federal tax lien, and its release$5.00, and $3.00
Assisted photocopy$2.00 per page
Self-service photocopy$0.25 per page
Certification$1.00 per document
Veterans discharge (DD-214), recording or certified copyNo fee

There is no reference fee on a master mortgage reference. Plats are priced by size, at ten cents per square inch with a $40.00 minimum per page, and the schedule lists three common sheet sizes with their totals.

sections.h2: What does the Lucas County Auditor charge before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Lucas County's Auditor publishes a real estate transfers fact sheet with two charges. The transfer fee is $0.50 per parcel. The conveyance fee is $4.00 for every $1,000 of the sale price, and some transfers outlined in law are exempt from it.

The sheet adds that transfers caused by a death, adding survivorship, or placing the property into your own trust are generally exempt and cost only the $0.50 per parcel. The Auditor cannot prepare a deed, and the sheet recommends hiring an attorney because a wrong detail can get the document rejected or cause trouble years later. The Auditor's main line is 419-213-4406.

The statewide rules behind these steps are in section 319.202, which requires the buyer's value statement before the Auditor endorses a deed, and section 319.54, which lists the exempt transfers.

sections.h2: How can I check a Lucas County deed online?
sections.html:
The Recorder's page says recorded documents after 1985 can be viewed through its Online Recordings tool, which is run by a document technology vendor. The Auditor's fact sheet points to the AREIS property system, where deeds and transfers are public.

AREIS shows how title is held, which helps when you are sorting out a sale after a death:

  • Property held in survivorship carries the code ORSURVTC after the owners' names.
  • Property held by a trustee shows the word Trustee after the name.
  • A transfer on death confirmation appears as document type OD on the Transfers page.

For records from before 1985, call the counter on 419-213-4400 and ask how to request a copy.

sections.h2: Why should I avoid paid deed retrieval companies in Lucas County?
sections.html:
Because the county sells the same copy for far less. The Recorder's news section warns residents about solicitations from document retrieval companies that quote $49.50 to $87.00 for a certified copy of a deed. It adds that copies of all land records are available from the office, often for as little as $2.00.

The fee schedule backs that up: assisted copies are $2.00 per page and a certification is $1.00 per document. A copy order form can be emailed to the Recorder or faxed to 419-213-4284 if you have an escrow account with the office. Copies are paid by cash, check or escrow account only.

sections.h2: What does Lucas County look like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Lucas County covers 596 square miles of northwest Ohio, of which 255 square miles is water, along Lake Erie and the Maumee River, based on Wikipedia's county entry. Toledo is the county seat and largest city. The other cities are Maumee, Oregon, Sylvania and Waterville, and the villages include Holland, Ottawa Hills, Whitehouse and Swanton. Much of the land lay within the Great Black Swamp before settlement. I-75, I-475, I-280 and the Ohio Turnpike cross the county.

The Census Bureau reports 423,347 residents in July 2025, down 1.8 percent from the 2020 base, and 201,974 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 it shows a median owner-occupied value of $163,900, median household income of $62,224, owner occupancy of 62.0 percent and median gross rent of $934. With nearly four homes in ten rented, many Lucas County sales involve a tenant-occupied house.

sections.h2: Which documents does the Lucas County Recorder file besides deeds?
sections.html:
The office's overview lists the full range of paperwork it accepts for the permanent land record:

  • Certificates of transfer, deeds and land contracts.
  • Mortgages, liens and real estate financing statements.
  • Plats and powers of attorney.
  • Military service discharges, and any other document made recordable by the Revised Code.

For lien paperwork the schedule gives $5.00 for a federal tax lien, $3.00 for its release and $4.00 for a personal tax release. Bureau of Workers' Compensation liens and releases carry no fee. The e-recording partners also list direct lines: CSC at 866-652-0111, ePN at 888-325-3365 extension 11234, and Simplifile at 800-460-5657 extension 1031.

sections.h2: How did Lucas County's recording fee reach its present level?
sections.html:
The Recorder's news section tracks two jumps. On October 17, 2019, the state budget raised the fee for most documents by $6.00, to $34.00 for the first two pages, with half of all recording fees going to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund. The later $5.00 increase came from Senate Bill 94 and brought the figure to $39.00, under section 317.32.

The office also posted a postage change for mailed recordings. From August 17, 2026, the postage for a standard one ounce first class letter rose from $.80 to $1.00, and that amount should be included whenever no self addressed stamped envelope is enclosed. Counting a mailed deed's return postage in the payment avoids a delay at intake.

sections.h2: How did Lucas County come to exist, and why does it matter for a title search?
sections.html:
Lucas County was organized in 1835 and named for the governor of Ohio at the time. Its creation was tied to the Toledo War, because both Ohio and Michigan Territory claimed a strip of land along the border. Earlier, the Battle of Fallen Timbers took place near present day Maumee in 1794.

For a seller, the practical point is that a title company orders the ownership search. The Recorder's online system covers documents recorded after 1985, so ask the title company how it will pull anything older.

faqs.q: How much is the basic recording fee in Lucas County?
faqs.a: The schedule lists $39.00 for the first two pages of a deed or mortgage, with $8.00 for each additional page. A document that breaks the state layout rules draws a $20.00 non-compliance fee, and each reference for a marginal notation costs $4.00.

faqs.q: What are the Lucas County transfer and conveyance fees?
faqs.a: The Auditor's fact sheet shows $0.50 per parcel as the transfer fee and $4.00 for every $1,000 of the sale price as the conveyance fee. Transfers due to death, survivorship or moving the property into your own trust are generally exempt from the conveyance fee.

faqs.q: Does the Lucas County Recorder accept mailed deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recorder encourages mailing and e-recording. Include a self addressed stamped envelope or add return postage to the payment, and make the check payable to the Lucas County Recorder.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a veteran's discharge in Lucas County?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule lists no fee to record a DD-214 or to get certified copies of it from the Recorder.

faqs.q: Can the Lucas County Auditor prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. The Auditor's fact sheet says the office cannot prepare transfer documents, including deeds, and recommends hiring an attorney. Staff can answer questions about the transfer process at 419-213-4406.
